Global Data Privacy Compliance Assessment Engine
Step 1 — Setup
WHY WE ASKThe regulation decides which controls, legal references and penalties the assessment uses. Everything that follows, from the questions to the wording of the report, is built on this choice.HOW TO ANSWER
DPDP ACTChoose this for processing digital personal data in India, or offering goods or services to people in India. It is the default for this tool.
OTHER LAWChoose another regime only when you are assessing against that law. Each assessment covers one regulation, so run a separate one for each.
WHY WE ASKThe name appears on the cover of the report and on any saved comparison, so it should match the entity being assessed.HOW TO ANSWER
LEGAL NAMEUse the registered or trading name, for example “Acme Financial Services Pvt Ltd”.
GROUPIf several entities decide why and how personal data is used, assess each one separately.
WHY WE ASKThe report names the person who completed the assessment, so readers know who is accountable for the answers and whom to contact.HOW TO ANSWER
WHOEnter the person answering the questions, typically the DPO, privacy lead or business owner.
SEVERAL PEOPLEIf several people contribute, enter the person who signs off the final answers.
WHY WE ASKYour industry sets the privacy profile below, so you get the controls and rules that fit how your business handles personal data. It also appears on your report.HOW TO ANSWER
NOT LISTEDChoose “My industry is not listed” and pick the closest privacy profile yourself.
WHY WE ASKThe privacy profile groups industries that handle personal data in similar ways. It adds sector controls on top of the baseline and shapes the sector considerations in the report. Picking your industry sets it for you.HOW TO ANSWER
CLOSEST MATCHPick your industry first; the profile is set automatically. Change it only if your data looks more like another profile.
MIXED BUSINESSPick the profile that covers your most sensitive data, such as health or finance. Choose “Other” if nothing fits.
WHY WE ASKEvery organisation owes the baseline duties, but how formal a control needs to be grows with scale. Controls that only make sense at higher volumes are deferred and listed in the report, and no legal duty is removed.HOW TO ANSWER
HOW TO COUNTEstimate the distinct individuals whose data you hold: customers, employees, leads and vendors combined.
NOT SUREChoose the nearest band. If you are torn between two, take the higher one; it only adds controls and never removes a duty.
Heightened obligations *
WHY WE ASKOrganisations designated as higher-risk carry extra duties, such as a DPO based in India, periodic impact assessments and independent audits. Saying Yes adds that group of controls to your assessment.HOW TO ANSWER
YESChoose Yes if you have been designated, or you want to be assessed against these duties in advance. Financial-sector and large-scale processors are the likeliest candidates.
NOChoose No if you have not been designated and are assessing the baseline duties only. You can run the assessment again later with Yes.

Quick check · about 5 minutes

Quick know-how check

Fourteen short multiple-choice questions on the points most often got wrong. Answer them all and you get a sample report on your understanding, with the correct answer and the reasoning behind each one. It tests knowledge only: it is separate from the compliance assessment and does not change its score.

0 of 14 answered
Free check · about 2 minutes

DPDP Exposure Check

Eight to ten quick questions about the personal data your business holds and how it moves, including one or two specific to your sector. Your business name, sector and scale come from Setup, so they are not asked again. You get a short report on how exposed the business is under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, which duties apply to you, and what to do next. It measures exposure, not compliance: it does not ask about or score your controls.

Portfolio view

Multi-client comparison

Compare several organisations side by side. Add the current assessment, or import saved .json files for other clients. Comparisons stay on this device only.

Progress over time

Client trend & improvement

Re-assess the same client on different dates and add each one to the comparison — this view charts how their maturity changes over time. Add at least two assessments of one organisation to see a trend.

Scoring configuration

Control weighting editor

Adjust how heavily each control counts toward the score and how severe its gaps are. Standard = weight 1, Critical = weight 2, Mandatory = weight 3. Changes apply consistently across every client and re-assessment, on this device.

Analysis

Insights & analysis

A data-driven read of the current assessment — systemic themes, quick wins versus strategic priorities, and a sequenced 30 / 60 / 90-day plan.

Ground validation

Personal Data Discovery

Three layers that a control questionnaire cannot reach: what personal data the organisation really holds, how well the team understands the DPDP Act, and what it could actually evidence if the Board asked tomorrow. Answer from today's reality, not from the plan.

Ground validation

Ground-validation report

Methodology

The assessment standard

The published method behind every score in this engine — domains, rating scales, evidence expectations, sampling, weighting and the conformity criteria. Share it with clients so results are transparent and repeatable.

Deep research

Privacy knowledge base

Per-domain research briefs: the statutory basis, what good looks like, the evidence to collect, and common pitfalls. Use these to brief clients, scope an audit, or justify findings.
